Modal screens and dialogs

Source: R/screens.R
modal.Rd

modal() builds a screen that is drawn over the current one and takes the keyboard and mouse until it is closed. Show it with app$push_screen(); close it with Escape or screen$dismiss(result). The previously focused widget gets focus back.

Usage

modal(
  ...,
  title = NULL,
  width = 50L,
  dim = TRUE,
  dismissable = TRUE,
  on_dismiss = NULL,
  id = NULL
)

confirm_dialog(
  message,
  on_confirm = NULL,
  on_cancel = NULL,
  title = "Confirm",
  confirm_label = "OK",
  cancel_label = "Cancel",
  width = 50L
)

alert_dialog(message, title = "Message", button_label = "OK", width = 50L)

Arguments

...

Content widgets (placed in a bordered panel).

title

Panel title.

width

Panel width (cells, "auto", "50%", ...).

dim

Dim the screens below?

dismissable

Can Escape close the dialog?

on_dismiss

function(result, app) called when the dialog closes.

id

Optional identifier of the screen.

message

Message text.

on_confirm, on_cancel

function(app) called when the user confirms, or cancels (Cancel button or Escape).

confirm_label, cancel_label

Button labels.

button_label

Label of the close button.

Value

A ModalScreen.

Details

confirm_dialog() and alert_dialog() are ready-made dialogs built on modal().

Examples

dlg <- confirm_dialog("Delete file?", on_confirm = function(app) message("deleted"))
a <- app(label("main"))
pilot <- test_app(a, 40, 10)
a$push_screen(dlg)
pilot$press("tab", "enter") # move to OK, press it
#> deleted
pilot$stop()
